title: Harbor Crest Realty site + listings refresh: neutralise a mixed-light listing batch to one house look against an in-frame grey card, match-grade a licensed stock hero to the same white point, cut the responsive web set, triage the two brand marks, and data-merge a featured-listings proof book
grounding_note: ADAPTED from the real Freelancer.com 'Vibrant Social & Web Graphics' brief: the client wants 'matching website graphics — hero images, section headers, and call-to-action spots — plus occasional banner ads for promotional campaigns'; every asset should 'feel part of one cohesive family while being perfectly sized, compressed, and formatted for its destination'; deliverables include 'Web-ready exports in the correct dimensions and file types' and a 'Mini style reference (colours, typography) to keep future assets consistent.' The real posting names no client and attaches no images, so the brand is laundered to a FICTIONAL boutique waterfront-and-city brokerage, 'Harbor Crest Realty', with a fictional persona (marketing lead Priya Deshmukh). No real company, person, brokerage, marketplace, software or trademark is named anywhere; only Adobe's own products (Adobe Stock, Creative Cloud, the platform) and the sourcing site (Freelancer.com, as source.platform provenance) appear. STRENGTHENED to remove the killed single-hero defects: the prior version (1) licensed ONE stock photo and cropped it seven ways — breadth, not depth, with the whole difficulty sitting in seven near-identical crop calls and no cross-asset consistency to measure; (2) had NO failure gate the agent could trip (open-loop 'apply the slider in the stated direction'); (3) delegated the designed artifact to a plumbing folder-upload hand-off; (4) used deprecated tool names (image_adjust_color_temperature / _highlights / _vibrance_and_saturation). The job is preserved and the bar raised: the brokerage supplies its OWN batch of six listing photographs shot across several homes under deliberately different light (each with the photographer's neutral grey/white-balance card clipped in frame) that must be neutralised BY EYE to one Harbor Crest house look; it ALSO licenses one large aspirational Adobe Stock architecture hero (asset_search → asset_license_and_download_stock) that must be match-graded to the SAME house white point (judged on its in-frame natural neutral — white trim / white cabinetry) and reframed DOWN into the desktop / tablet / mobile web heroes, two section headers and two promo banners — never upscaled or generatively expanded; the two client brand marks are triaged (a flat wordmark vectorized vs a photographed embossed brass seal kept as raster); and the whole thing ends in a genuinely agent-owned designed artifact — a one-record-per-page data-merge of the graded listings + copy roster through a hand-authored .indd into a single press-ready featured-listings proof book. NO from-scratch illustration, NO generative fill/expand/outpaint, NO upscaling: every visual is a licensed-and-cropped-DOWN stock frame, a graded owned listing photo, or a client raster that is only knocked-out / vectorized.
one_line_ask: Neutralise six differently-lit Harbor Crest listing photos to the grey card each carries (by eye) and grade them to one house look, license one large Adobe Stock architecture hero and match-grade it to the SAME house white point on its own in-frame natural neutral, cut that graded hero DOWN into a desktop / tablet / mobile web hero, two section-header strips and two promo banners (one given a navy monochromatic treatment), decide which of the two supplied brand marks can become clean vector line art and which must stay a photographic raster, recommend an on-brand type pairing, then data-merge the graded listings and copy roster through the authored template into one press-ready featured-listings proof book — one listing per page — and report the per-image corrections you applied.
full_brief:
Harbor Crest Realty is a fictional boutique waterfront-and-city brokerage refreshing both its website imagery and its printed listing leave-behind. Our site structure and copy already work; the imagery feels dated and mismatched and no longer signals the premium, trustworthy feel we want. We are NOT building the website here — our developer handles the build — we need the finished, cohesive imagery plus a listings proof book we can sign off in a partners' meeting. The whole thing has to read as ONE brand: one light, one warmth, one premium mood, top to bottom.

FIRST, our own listing photography. We are handing you six photos our agents shot across six different homes over the last month (roughly 4000px, straight off the camera). They do NOT match: every room was lit by whatever was there — warm ceiling downlights, a cool north-facing window, old kitchen fluorescents, a mixed window-and-lamp split, one dim twilight exterior, one exterior caught in strong late light. Because we knew the light was a mess, our photographer clipped a neutral grey balance card (a mid-grey patch beside a white patch) into every frame. Use that card as your ground truth: every listing photo has to be neutralised so the card reads truly neutral — no residual warm, blue or green cast — and so the card's mid-grey sits at the same brightness across all six, then carried to ONE Harbor Crest house look: clean, warm-but-not-orange, shadows open so interiors read airy, whites held so windows keep detail, a restrained premium pop. Here is the craft, and it is where our last editor failed: the six did NOT start from the same place, so there is no single correction that fixes them — a move that rescues one frame drives another further off. Judge each frame by eye off its own card, work out what is actually wrong with THAT frame, choose the right control to neutralise it, and dial that frame its own correction until all six cards land on the same neutral and the same mid-grey. Do NOT reach for one global white-balance number, do NOT copy one frame's settings onto the others, and do NOT just auto-tone each one to look fine alone — auto-tone keys off each frame's own histogram, so the casts will not agree and the set will visibly fail to match at the card, and we will reject it. And read each frame honestly: if a frame already reads on our warm house look, do not push it further to chase a mood — match it to the set, do not overcook it. The look itself is yours to build from scratch and hold identical across the set; there is no preset to lean on, only our one-page house-look target (neutral card + whites-held + open shadows + gentle contrast + restrained warmth).

SECOND, the website hero imagery. We do not have a wide, aspirational hero shot of our own, so license one from Adobe Stock: a high-quality modern light-filled living space or a clean contemporary home exterior in warm natural light, no recognisable faces, no readable signage, and licensed LARGE — big enough (roughly 5000px on the long edge) that you can cut several web slots out of it without ever enlarging it. That stock hero has to belong to the same family as our listings, so match-grade it to the SAME house white point you established on the listing batch — but the stock frame has no grey card, so judge it on its own natural neutral (the white trim, white cabinetry or white parasols in the shot) until it sits on the same warm-white as the set. From that one graded master, cut our web slots, each perfectly sized for its destination and each framed so the architecture survives the reframe: a desktop hero 2560x1080, a tablet hero 1536x1024, a mobile hero 1080x1350, two low-band section-header strips 1920x480 for the 'Featured Listings' and 'About Us' sections, a leaderboard promo banner 1200x628, and a square promo 1080x1080 — and give the square one a subtle navy monochromatic treatment so it reads as the stylised promo variant rather than a plain photo. Every one of those is cut DOWN from the big licensed master — never stretched, never AI-expanded.

THIRD, our two brand marks, which are NOT the same kind of file and must not be treated the same. We are handing you two of them. One can become clean, razor-sharp vector line art for every masthead and print corner; the other cannot survive being turned into flat line art and has to stay a photographic raster with its real surface intact. Work out which is which, prep each the right way, and hand back the vector as an SVG and the raster as a transparent-background PNG. (One of them will need straightening and cleaning before it can be traced at all — do not trace it raw.)

FOURTH, the sign-off artifact. We have hand-built the featured-listings card template (a genuine authored .indd) with live placeholder fields and three image slots — the listing photo, the wordmark masthead and the corner seal — and we are giving you the six-listing roster with our addresses, prices and headline copy. Merge them so every listing gets its own proof page with its copy bound, its matching graded photo placed, the crisp vector wordmark in the masthead and the seal in the corner, then hand back one press-ready featured-listings proof book, one listing per page, for the partners' deck. Bind our copy verbatim from the roster; do not rewrite it. Finally, recommend an on-brand heading/label typeface pairing for the mini style reference.

Deliverables: the six graded listing masters (as a contact set we can eyeball against the card), the graded stock hero master, the responsive web set (desktop/tablet/mobile heroes, two section headers, leaderboard + navy square banner), the wordmark SVG and the seal PNG prepped the correct way each, the font-pairing note, the press-ready featured-listings proof book (one listing per page), and a short note listing the final white-balance and exposure move you applied to each of the six listing photos and to the stock hero — so we can confirm the set was matched to the card, not just eyeballed. Everything must feel part of one family.

inputs.name: listing_ref_01.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL straight-off-camera interior real-estate listing photograph of a staged open-plan living room with a sofa, coffee table and large window, ~4000px on the long edge, 3:2 landscape. Lit by WARM tungsten ceiling downlights and slightly OVER-exposed, so the whole frame carries an amber cast and reads a touch hot. A neutral grey balance card (a mid-grey patch beside a small white patch) is clipped to a light stand or propped on the coffee table, clearly visible in the lower frame. Real furniture, floor and wall texture, natural window falloff, no people, no readable signage, un-graded documentary listing look.
inputs.realism_notes: Batch member 1 and the 'Harbourfront Loft' listing. Deliberately WARM and slightly over, so the correct move toward the house look is COOL-to-neutral plus a small exposure pull-down — the OPPOSITE of the cool frames. The in-frame grey card is the neutralisation ground truth; the retained graded master keeps the card in frame for the grader, while the merged listing crop excludes it. Camera-scale (~4000px) so its print listing-card crop (~2600x1500) is a downscale.

inputs.name: listing_ref_02.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL straight-off-camera interior real-estate listing photograph of a staged primary bedroom with a made bed and a large north-facing window, ~4000px long edge, 3:2 landscape. Shot in COOL north-window daylight and slightly UNDER-exposed, so the whole frame reads blue and a touch dark, flat contrast. A neutral grey balance card (mid-grey patch beside a white patch) is propped on the windowsill or nightstand, clearly visible. Real bedding, timber and wall texture, no people, no readable signage, un-graded documentary look.
inputs.realism_notes: Batch member 2, the 'Northgate Bungalow' listing. Cool + under: the OPPOSITE corrective direction to listing_ref_01, so a single shared white balance cannot neutralise both — this is the identical-params trap. Its correction is a WARM shift plus an exposure LIFT to the card. Camera-scale so its listing-card crop downscales.

inputs.name: listing_ref_03.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL straight-off-camera interior real-estate listing photograph of a staged kitchen with cabinetry, a counter and a backsplash, ~4000px long edge, 3:2 landscape. Lit by old overhead GREEN fluorescent tubes so the whole frame carries a distinct sickly green cast, normal exposure, slightly dull. A neutral grey balance card (mid-grey patch beside a white patch) is propped on the counter, clearly visible and visibly skewing green. Real cabinet, stone-counter and tile texture, no people, no readable signage, un-graded look.
inputs.realism_notes: Batch member 3, the 'Saltmarsh Cottage' listing. The green fluorescent cast is on the TINT axis, not the temperature axis — a warm/cool move will never clear it; the correct neutralisation pushes TINT toward MAGENTA with only a small temperature trim. It is the frame that most cleanly exposes a one-global-WB or temperature-only or per-frame-auto-tone approach, because those cannot touch a green cast at all, so its card stays green while the others look fixed. White cabinetry doubles as a second natural neutral. Camera-scale.

inputs.name: listing_ref_04.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL straight-off-camera interior real-estate listing photograph of a staged ensuite bathroom with a vanity, mirror and a window on one side, ~4000px long edge, 3:2 landscape. Lit by a MIX of cool window light on one side and a warm vanity bulb on the other, so the cast is split and uneven across the frame, normal exposure, flat contrast. A neutral grey balance card (mid-grey patch beside a white patch) is propped on the vanity, clearly visible. Real tile, glass and chrome texture, no people, no readable signage, un-graded look.
inputs.realism_notes: Batch member 4, the 'Pier View Flat' listing. Split/mixed cast is the hardest to neutralise: the agent must average toward the card's neutral rather than fully killing one side (drive the card grey neutral even if one wall stays slightly warmer). A different reasoning problem again — not a single-direction WB nudge. Camera-scale.

inputs.name: listing_ref_05.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL straight-off-camera exterior real-estate listing photograph of a contemporary home facade at dusk, ~4000px long edge, 3:2 landscape. Clearly UNDER-exposed / dim twilight, the facade and driveway reading muddy and dark, faint cool cast, real render of cladding, glass and landscaping texture, no people, no readable signage. A neutral grey balance card (mid-grey patch beside a white patch) is propped on a low wall or step near the door, sitting dark but visible. Un-graded documentary look.
inputs.realism_notes: Batch member 5, the 'Cliffside Villa' listing. The exposure-rescue frame: a large exposure + shadow lift to bring the facade and the card up to legibility, held in check by pulling highlights/whites so the recovered sky/lit windows do not blow past clipping and the dark areas stay off pure black — a single reasoned exposure-rescue of unique magnitude, so copying any other frame's numbers here visibly under- or over-shoots. Camera-scale.

inputs.name: listing_ref_06.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL straight-off-camera exterior real-estate listing photograph of a whitewashed / light-clad home with white trim and a porch in strong late-afternoon natural light, ~4000px long edge, 3:2 landscape. It is well-exposed and its white trim and light cladding ALREADY read as a warm sun-washed white that sits right on a warm house look — the warmth is the real late light, correctly captured, NOT a white-balance error. A neutral grey balance card (mid-grey patch beside a white patch) is propped on the porch step, clearly visible and already reading close to neutral. Real cladding, trim and foliage texture, no people, no readable signage, un-graded look.
inputs.realism_notes: Batch member 6, the 'Harbour House' listing, and THE UNDISCLOSED TRAP frame. It looks like the frame that should be pushed hardest to look 'warm and inviting', but its white trim and card ALREADY sit on the house warm-white and it is correctly exposed. The correct move is to HOLD white balance (at most a tiny cool nudge to sit exactly on the set target) and only match exposure and the black-point to the rest; warming it further to chase the golden light drives its trim off-neutral orange and breaks the set match. The brief states only the goal (one house look, match don't overcook) and never discloses that this frame is already on target — a naive agent that warms everything to 'golden and inviting' fails here. Camera-scale.

inputs.name: harbor_stock_search_intent.json
inputs.gen_prompt: Output a short JSON object describing the Adobe Stock search a real-estate marketing lead would run for a large website hero, e.g. {"query":"modern light-filled open-plan living space with floor-to-ceiling windows and white trim in warm natural light, contemporary architecture, no people","orientation":"landscape","min_resolution":"5000x3333","license":"standard","mood":"premium, aspirational, warm, trustworthy","exclusions":"no faces, no visible signage or logos, no text overlays"}. This is the client's creative direction expressed as a stock query and drives asset_search / asset_license_and_download_stock. It deliberately calls out white trim / white cabinetry in the scene, because that natural neutral is what the stock hero (which carries no grey card) is match-graded against.
inputs.realism_notes: Represents Harbor Crest's creative direction, not a pixel asset. The min_resolution ~5000px is deliberately large so the chain can CROP multiple web slots DOWN from one master rather than expand a small file. The 'white trim / white cabinetry' note tells the agent what natural neutral to grade the card-less stock hero on, so it lands on the same house white point as the carded listing batch.

inputs.name: harbor_mark_A.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat desktop scan of a real-estate wordmark lockup printed on off-white textured paper: an elegant high-contrast deep-navy serif wordmark reading 'HARBOR CREST REALTY' with a small simple line-drawn cresting-wave / lighthouse glyph to the left, single deep-navy ink on a slightly warm off-white paper ground (NOT transparent, NOT pure white). The whole mark sits very slightly rotated (~2 degrees) on the scan bed, there is extra paper margin around it, and edges are a touch soft as a real scan would be. High enough contrast that, once cleaned and straightened, it will vectorize cleanly.
inputs.realism_notes: One of the two brand marks, supplied under a NEUTRAL name (mark_A) so the agent must open it to decide its treatment. This one is flat, high-contrast single-colour line art on an off-white ground, so it CAN become clean vector — but only after prep-before-trace: straighten the ~2 degree skew, crisp it, crop to the mark, knock the off-white ground to transparency, THEN vectorize. Fed raw, image_vectorize would trace the paper and bake in the skew. Its enclosed letter-counters trace filled-white on the off-white ground and read correctly on the template's LIGHT cream masthead panel — no dark-ground knockout is claimed. Do NOT let the filename or the brief say which mark this is; the triage is the agent's to make.

inputs.name: harbor_mark_B.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A close-up PHOTOGRAPH of a small embossed brass founder's / accreditation seal-medallion reading 'HARBOR CREST · EST. MMXIV' around a raised wave relief, shot on a dark surface: shiny metallic brass with specular highlights, soft reflections, raised embossed relief and smooth tonal gradients across the metal. Clearly a photographed glossy metal object, not flat line art — full of sheen and gradient.
inputs.realism_notes: The other brand mark, also under a NEUTRAL name (mark_B), and the TRIAGE / TRAP mark. It looks like 'just the other logo', but it is a photographed metallic surface full of gradients and specular sheen: feeding it to image_vectorize returns a flat, muddy silhouette that destroys the brass. The correct treatment is crop-to-bounds → image_remove_background to transparency → keep as a high-resolution RASTER placed via @Seal. Getting it wrong is invisible in a thumbnail and only shows when the seal prints flat and dead on the proof. The mark that CANNOT survive a trace.

inputs.name: harbor_listings_roster.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a CSV with headers exactly: listing,address,price,beds_baths,headline,subhead,@Photo,@Wordmark,@Seal and 6 rows, one per listing, in this order: (1) listing 'Harbourfront Loft', address '14 Wharfside Lane', price '$865,000', beds_baths '2 bed · 2 bath', headline 'Light Above the Water', subhead 'An open-plan loft with the harbour at the window.', @Photo 'listing_harbourfront_loft.jpg'; (2) listing 'Northgate Bungalow', address '6 Saltmarsh Row', price '$740,000', beds_baths '3 bed · 2 bath', headline 'Quiet Mornings, North Light', subhead 'A calm bungalow on a leafy northside street.', @Photo 'listing_northgate_bungalow.jpg'; (3) listing 'Saltmarsh Cottage', address '9 Cove End', price '$695,000', beds_baths '2 bed · 1 bath', headline 'A Cottage by the Marsh', subhead 'Warm timber and a cook''s kitchen near the shore.', @Photo 'listing_saltmarsh_cottage.jpg'; (4) listing 'Pier View Flat', address '3 Pier View, Unit 5', price '$520,000', beds_baths '1 bed · 1 bath', headline 'Steps From the Pier', subhead 'A bright flat with a spa-style ensuite.', @Photo 'listing_pier_view_flat.jpg'; (5) listing 'Cliffside Villa', address '28 Beacon Rise', price '$1,240,000', beds_baths '4 bed · 3 bath', headline 'The Cliffside Villa', subhead 'Contemporary lines above the coast road.', @Photo 'listing_cliffside_villa.jpg'; (6) listing 'Harbour House', address '11 Crest Terrace', price '$980,000', beds_baths '3 bed · 2 bath', headline 'Sun on the Porch', subhead 'A white-clad classic with all-day light.', @Photo 'listing_harbour_house.jpg'. The @Wordmark column holds the SAME file 'harbor_logo.svg' in EVERY row and the @Seal column holds the SAME file 'harbor_seal.png' in EVERY row, so the merge drops the two shared brand marks onto every listing page as merge binds (never free-form placement). The @Photo column holds each listing's DISTINCT graded photo filename (the agent must produce and upload each graded listing crop under these exact names). Column names must exactly match the template merge fields <<listing>>,<<address>>,<<price>>,<<beds_baths>>,<<headline>>,<<subhead>> and the three @image-path columns @Photo,@Wordmark,@Seal.
inputs.realism_notes: Six rows => the merge must produce exactly six finished proof pages (page-count = row-count gate). @Photo carries a DISTINCT listing filename per row (the graded owned photos the agent produces), while @Wordmark and @Seal carry the identical shared marks in all six rows — proving all three image columns land in the deliverable and giving the vectorized wordmark and the raster seal a real, connector-doable path onto every page with no free-form image-at-coordinates placement. NO column encodes a lighting cast or a treatment — the CSV states only listing copy (the goal); the per-frame diagnosis lives only in each input's realism_notes and the step notes. Addresses/prices are fictional. Copy binds verbatim; the agent does not rewrite it.

inputs.name: harbor_featured_listings_template.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (cannot be model-generated): a genuine, hand-built page-layout document (.indd/.idml) for a SINGLE-RECORD US-Letter-portrait (216 x 279 mm) featured-listing proof card with 3 mm bleed — ONE listing per page. It must contain live data-merge placeholder fields <<listing>>, <<address>>, <<price>>, <<beds_baths>>, <<headline>>, <<subhead>>, AND three @-prefixed image-path merge columns wired to three separate image frames: a large upper listing-photo frame (~223 x 133 mm bleed edge, i.e. ~2632 x 1571 px at ~300 DPI) bound to @Photo (that listing's graded owned photo, cut DOWN from the ~4000 px source so filling the frame is a DOWNSCALE at ~300 DPI — never enlarged), a small light CREAM masthead panel with a logo frame bound to @Wordmark (the vectorized wordmark), and a lower-corner frame bound to @Seal (the transparent-ground brass seal). The masthead panel behind @Wordmark is a LIGHT cream band (so the vectorized wordmark's enclosed letter-counters, which trace filled-white on their off-white ground, read correctly on light — never a dark-ground knockout). Because free-form image-at-coordinates placement is banned, the wordmark and seal reach every page ONLY as merge binds through these image columns. Built by hand so the text fields and all THREE image fields actually bind. Explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output (a converted PDF has no live merge fields and no data-merge image fields, so it would not bind) and NOT a multi-up sheet: document_merge_data_layout emits one page per row, so the template holds exactly one listing's worth of fields.
inputs.realism_notes: document_merge_data_layout is [T] and REQUIRES a user-authored .indd/.idml carrying real merge fields plus genuine @image-path columns, and it produces ONE FILE PER ROW — so a single-record per-listing card is the correct, connector-doable shape. Supplied as an input, not a chain output. THREE image columns (@Photo distinct per row, @Wordmark and @Seal identical across all rows) mean the merge resolves three prepped assets per page — the listing's own graded photo plus the two shared brand marks — giving the chain-produced wordmark and seal a real, connector-doable path onto every page with no free-form placement (mirrors AO-74's @image/@Wordmark and AO-117's @Hero/@Wordmark/@Seal three-image-column patterns).

inputs.name: harbor_brand_kit.json
inputs.gen_prompt: Output a small JSON brand sheet for the fictional brokerage: {"brand":"Harbor Crest Realty","contact":"Priya Deshmukh, Marketing Lead","navy":"#17324B","sand":"#C9A66B","offwhite":"#F5F1E8","voice":"premium, calm, trustworthy, coastal","house_look":"neutral to the in-frame grey card, whites held below clipping, shadows open, gentle contrast, restrained warmth — warm but never orange","web_slots":{"desktop_hero":"2560x1080","tablet_hero":"1536x1024","mobile_hero":"1080x1350","section_header":"1920x480","banner_leaderboard":"1200x628","banner_square":"1080x1080"},"note":"one cohesive family; listings and the licensed stock hero graded to the same white point; correct dimensions per destination"}. These are the brand colours, contact persona, house-look target and required web dimensions the brief implies.
inputs.realism_notes: The 'mini style reference' the brief names, expressed as a brand sheet; it states the house-look target qualitatively (neutral-to-card, whites-held, warm-not-orange) — NOT a pixel hex the agent must match by measuring — and carries the navy hue for the square banner treatment and the exact web slot sizes. Drives font_recommend and the applied-parameters note. IP-clean fictional brand + persona.

outputs.name: listing_masters_graded_x6
outputs.spec: The six listing photos graded as one matched set, each corrected on its OWN terms — the warm frame cooled, the cool frame warmed and lifted, the green kitchen pushed on the TINT axis toward magenta, the mixed frame compromised to neutral, the twilight exterior exposure-rescued, and the already-on-target sun-lit exterior HELD on white balance and only tone-matched — so each frame's in-frame grey card reads true-neutral and its mid patch matches the set mid-grey, whites held below clipping and blacks off pure black, then the single authored Harbor Crest house look (gentle contrast + open shadows + restrained warmth, built from primitive adjustments, no preset, no auto-tone) held identical across all six. These are the RETAINED card-bearing masters (the grey card still in frame), ~4000px, the artifacts the match is graded on. Acceptance (grader-checked, on these retained masters): every frame's grey card reads neutral within a tight channel-spread tolerance with the mid patch on a shared mid-grey, whites below the clip ceiling and blacks off pure black; the agent never measures — it neutralises by eye and the grader measures the card.

outputs.name: hero_master_graded.jpg
outputs.spec: The licensed Adobe Stock architecture hero (~5000px landscape) match-graded to the SAME Harbor Crest house white point as the listing batch — judged on its in-frame natural neutral (white trim / white cabinetry / white parasols) rather than a grey card, since stock carries none — warm-white on the trim consistent with the set, whites held, shadows open. The single retained master every web slot is cropped DOWN from. Acceptance (grader-checked): its white-trim natural-neutral reference reads the same warm-white as the listing set's cards, so the stock hero and the owned photography read as one family.

outputs.name: web_responsive_set
outputs.spec: The website hero family, all cut DOWN from hero_master_graded.jpg (existing pixels only, never enlarged, never canvas-extended): a desktop hero 2560x1080 (~21:9), a tablet hero 1536x1024, a mobile hero 1080x1350 (4:5 portrait), two low-band section-header strips 1920x480 ('Featured Listings' and 'About Us', different bands of the same master so they vary but stay in-family), and a leaderboard promo banner 1200x628 — each framed so the focal architecture survives the reframe, sRGB PNG, web-ready. Acceptance (grader-checked): every slot is at its exact listed pixel size and is a downscale from the ~5000px master (no upscaling anywhere).

outputs.name: banner_openhouse_square_navy.png
outputs.spec: Open-house promo square banner, exactly 1080x1080, cropped DOWN from hero_master_graded.jpg then given a subtle navy (#17324B) whole-image monochromatic treatment via image_apply_monochromatic_tint so it reads as the stylised branded promo variant rather than a plain photo. sRGB PNG. Acceptance (grader-checked): a navy-toned monochrome derivative of the same graded master, exact 1080x1080, downscaled (not enlarged).

outputs.name: harbor_logo.svg
outputs.spec: Clean vector SVG of the wordmark, traced only AFTER the supplied scan is straightened, crisped, cropped to the mark and knocked to transparency — razor-sharp at masthead scale with no captured paper ground and no ~2 degree skew. Its counters read correctly on the template's light cream masthead panel. This is the mark the agent triaged as the one that CAN become clean vector line art.

outputs.name: harbor_seal.png
outputs.spec: The embossed brass seal, cropped to bounds and knocked to a transparent ground via image_remove_background, kept as a HIGH-RESOLUTION RASTER (>=300 px square, so it prints >=300 DPI at ~25 mm) with all its metallic sheen and relief intact — deliberately NOT vectorized (a trace would flatten the brass to a muddy silhouette). This is the mark the agent triaged as the one that CANNOT survive a trace. Placed on every proof page via @Seal.

outputs.name: font_pairing_recommendation.txt
outputs.spec: Recommended heading/label typeface pairing matching the premium coastal look, from font_recommend driven by the brand kit voice and palette, for the mini style reference (existing typefaces only, no letterform design).

outputs.name: HarborCrest_FeaturedListings_x6.pdf
outputs.spec: Exactly six press-ready US-Letter-portrait (216 x 279 mm) featured-listing proof pages — ONE single-record page per roster listing (page-count = row-count = 6) — exported in a SINGLE render call from the one-record-per-page data-merge with 3 mm bleed at ~300 DPI; each page binds its listing/address/price/beds_baths/headline/subhead verbatim from the roster, places that listing's graded owned photo in the large upper frame via @Photo (a downscale from the ~4000px source, ~300 DPI at the frame, grey card cropped OUT of the delivered crop), the vectorized wordmark in the cream masthead via @Wordmark, and the transparent brass seal in the corner via @Seal. The 'hero' listing (Harbourfront Loft) is simply page 1 of this book, not a separately exported file (document_render_layout exports the whole merged document, never one named record). This is the agent-owned designed endpoint. Acceptance (grader-checked): page-count = row-count = 6; each page carries the correct listing's graded photo (card excluded) plus the two triaged marks; if fewer pages, the merge collapsed rows and failed.

outputs.name: grade_params_report
outputs.spec: A short note (secondary to the images) the agent authors and returns listing, per listing photo (listing_ref_01..06) and for the stock hero, the final correction it APPLIED — temperature and tint direction and amount, exposure and highlight/shadow moves, contrast, clarity and restrained warmth it dialed — and naming which axis carried each frame (warm-to-neutral, cool-to-neutral-and-lift, magenta TINT for the green kitchen, mixed-compromise, exposure-rescue for the twilight exterior, and HELD white balance for the already-on-target sun-lit exterior). This is an APPLIED-settings log, not a measurement: the agent knows these values because it set them by eye. Acceptance (grader-checked): the seven reported corrections are non-identical and their directions match each frame's cast — in particular the green kitchen carries a tint (not a temperature) move, the warm and cool frames move in opposite temperature directions, and the already-on-target frame reports white balance essentially HELD.

connector_workflow.note: Ingest the six client listing photos, the two brand marks and the brand-kit + search-intent notes into the working project so every downstream edit runs against real asset references. Plumbing, not difficulty.

Grade listing_ref_01 (warm tungsten living room, slightly over). Judge the amber cast by eye off the in-frame grey card and COOL the temperature toward neutral (dial and record the temp; trim tint only if the card also skews green), pull exposure down a touch out of the hot baseline, then lay in the authored house look built here from primitives — gentle contrast, open shadows, whites held below the clip ceiling, blacks seated just off pure black, restrained warmth. Goal: the grey card looks neutral by eye and its mid patch reads at the set mid-grey. Single authored adjustment call, NOT a preset and NOT auto-tone. Retain the card in this master for grading. Report the move.

Grade listing_ref_02 (cool north-window bedroom, slightly under) — the OPPOSITE temperature move to l1: WARM the temperature toward the same neutral card target and LIFT exposure/shadows, then apply the identical house-look contrast/warmth character so it matches the set. Applying l1's cooling here would push this frame further blue and dark — judging the card by eye is what tells the agent to reverse direction. Report the warming and lift dialed.

Grade listing_ref_03 (green fluorescent kitchen) — the TINT-axis frame. This one does NOT move on the warm/cool axis: judge the green card by eye and push TINT toward MAGENTA to neutralise it (with only a small temperature trim), then seat the mid/whites/blacks on the shared target and apply the identical house look. A temperature-only correction, a single global WB copied from the warm or cool frames, or an auto-tone pass cannot clear a green cast at all — this frame's card would stay green while the others look fixed, which is the visible failure this gate catches. Report the magenta tint amount and confirm it is a tint (not a temperature) move.

Grade listing_ref_04 (mixed window+lamp split cast): balance temperature AND tint toward the card's neutral, accepting a compromise since the two sides disagree — drive the card grey neutral even if one wall stays slightly warmer. Shared house-look character. A frame the agent must reason about rather than slide one way. Report the compromise move.

Grade listing_ref_05 (underexposed twilight exterior) — the exposure-rescue frame: a large exposure + shadow lift to bring the facade and the card up to legibility, held in check by pulling highlights/whites so the recovered sky/lit windows do not blow past clipping and the dark areas stay off pure black, plus a slight warm toward neutral and the house-look character. The magnitude of this lift is unique to this frame; copying any other frame's exposure here visibly under- or over-shoots. Report the exposure/shadow/highlight moves dialed.

Grade listing_ref_06 (sun-lit exterior) — THE TRAP FRAME. Its white trim and its grey card ALREADY read on the house warm-white and it is correctly exposed. The correct move is to HOLD white balance (at most a tiny cool nudge to sit exactly on the set target) and only match exposure and the black-point to the rest. A naive agent that 'warms everything to look golden and inviting' (or copies l1's or l2's move) drives this frame's trim off-neutral orange and breaks the set match — the decision is driven by THIS frame's card and trim, not the batch mood. Report that white balance was essentially HELD and only tone matched.

Search Adobe Stock for a large, aspirational modern architecture hero (light-filled living space or clean exterior in warm natural light, white trim/cabinetry present as a natural neutral, no faces, no signage) using the client's creative direction; returns low-res candidate previews + asset IDs. Filter to large-resolution results (~5000px long edge) so the web slots can be cut DOWN without any expansion.

License the chosen candidate BEFORE editing and download the full-resolution (~5000px) presigned file — license before use. This large licensed photo is the single seed the web set is graded and cropped from; big enough that every slot is a downscale.

Match-grade the licensed stock hero to the SAME Harbor Crest house white point the listing batch established — but this frame has NO grey card, so judge it on its in-frame natural neutral (the white trim / white cabinetry) until it sits on the same warm-white as the set, whites held, shadows open, the same restrained house-look character. Its own temperature/exposure deltas, reasoned to its own trim — not copied from a listing frame. This is the retained graded hero master every web slot is cut DOWN from. Authored from primitives, NOT a preset, NOT auto-tone. Report the move.

Crop/reframe the graded hero master DOWN to the 2560x1080 desktop hero band, keeping the focal architecture and leaving copy space on one side. onSubjectClipping='extract', DOWNSCALE-only from the ~5000px master — never generative-expand, never enlarge.
Crop/reframe the SAME graded hero master DOWN to the 1536x1024 tablet hero. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

Crop/reframe the SAME graded hero master DOWN to the 1080x1350 (4:5) mobile portrait hero, focal area preserved. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only (a 1080x1350 portrait region fits inside the ~5000x3333 landscape master — no upscale).
Cut a 1920x480 low-band strip from the graded hero master for the 'Featured Listings' section header. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.
Cut a DIFFERENT 1920x480 low band from the same graded hero master for the 'About Us' section header so the two headers vary while staying in-family. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

Crop/reframe the graded hero master DOWN to the 1200x628 open-house leaderboard promo banner, subject reframed to keep one region clear for a live headline/CTA overlay. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.
Crop the graded hero master DOWN to a 1080x1080 square base for the open-house square promo banner. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only from the ~5000px master.

Lay a subtle navy #17324B WHOLE-IMAGE monochromatic treatment over the square base so it reads as the stylised branded promo variant rather than a plain photo (deliverable). image_apply_monochromatic_tint is whole-image (no mask) — valid here because the ENTIRE square becomes a navy-toned monochrome; this is not a masked recolor and not a split-tone.

Crop the graded l1 master DOWN to the listing-card photo, framing the room and EXCLUDING the grey card from the delivered crop, sized to the template's @Photo frame (~2632x1571 px, ~300 DPI). onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only from the ~4000px master. The card-bearing l1_graded master is retained for grading; neutrality is graded THERE, card-exclusion on this delivered crop is checked separately.
Crop graded l2 DOWN to the @Photo frame, grey card excluded from the delivered crop. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.
Crop graded l3 DOWN to the @Photo frame, grey card excluded. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.
Crop graded l4 DOWN to the @Photo frame, grey card excluded. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.
Crop graded l5 DOWN to the @Photo frame, grey card excluded. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

Crop graded l6 DOWN to the @Photo frame, grey card excluded. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. listing_harbourfront_loft.jpg ... listing_harbour_house.jpg are the six @Photo binds for the merge, each cut from its retained graded master.

TRIAGE branch A begins. The agent has decided mark_A is the flat single-colour wordmark that CAN become vector — but it sits ~2 degrees rotated on the scan bed, so straighten it FIRST (image_auto_straighten is the only tool that rectifies a tilt). Feeding the raw skewed scan to vectorize would bake in the rotation. Prep-before-trace step 1.

Prep-before-trace step 2: push contrast/clarity and drive the off-white paper toward clean white so the deep-navy lettering separates hard from the ground — a soft low-contrast scan traces into ragged, doubled edges.
Prep-before-trace step 3: crop away the scan margin to the tight bounds of the mark so vectorize traces only the wordmark, not the paper field.

Prep-before-trace step 4: knock the off-white paper ground to transparency so the trace captures the letterforms only, not a rectangle of paper. remove_background → transparency (NOT select→invert→fill). On the off-white ground the enclosed counters trace filled-white and read correctly on the template's LIGHT cream masthead panel — no dark-ground knockout is claimed.

Now trace the prepared raster (straightened, crisped, cropped, transparent) into a clean SVG for the mastheads and print corners. Tracing the raw scan instead would produce a skewed, paper-bounded, fuzzy silhouette — the trap this prep chain avoids. mark_A is the mark that CAN become clean vector.

TRIAGE branch B DIVERGES here. The agent has decided mark_B is the PHOTOGRAPH of an embossed brass seal — full of sheen, reflections and relief gradients — so it CANNOT become clean line art (vectorizing it would return a flat muddy silhouette and kill the brass). Crop only to the tight bounds of the medallion; do NOT send it to image_vectorize.

Knock the dark surround to transparency so only the brass seal remains, keeping every specular highlight and relief gradient intact. remove_background → transparency (outer background only; NOT select→invert→fill, NOT a solid fill, no enclosed-interior hole claimed). This preserves the metallic sheen a vector path would have destroyed.

Square-crop/resize the transparent brass seal to a 1:1 corner mark at >=300 px square so it prints >=300 DPI at ~25 mm. Kept as a HIGH-RESOLUTION RASTER placed via @Seal on every page. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only — never enlarged past the photographed source. mark_B is the mark that CANNOT survive a trace.
Recommend an on-brand premium/coastal heading + label typeface pairing (existing typefaces only) for the mini style reference, driven by the brand kit voice and palette. No letterform design.

chaining_note: Strict output→input chaining throughout. asset_add_file(1) makes the six listing photos, the two brand marks and the notes real references. The six listing grades fan out from supplied_assets_uploaded but each is a DIFFERENT authored correction driven to a common in-frame grey-card target, not a repeated identical call: l1 warm-to-neutral (2), l2 cool-to-neutral-and-lift (3, opposite direction), l3 a magenta TINT for the green kitchen (4, a move the temperature frames never make), l4 a mixed-cast compromise (5), l5 an exposure-rescue of unique magnitude (6), l6 white-balance HELD for the already-on-target frame (7, the trap). The stock hero is a separate tributary: asset_search(8)→asset_license_and_download_stock(9)→match-grade to the SAME house white point on its own natural neutral (10). That one graded hero master then forks into seven web crops consuming only that master — desktop(11), tablet(12), mobile(13), two section headers(14,15), leaderboard(16), and a square base(17)→monochromatic navy(18) — all DOWNSCALE-only. Each graded listing master forks into its card-excluded @Photo crop for the merge: l1→(19), l2→(20), l3→(21), l4→(22), l5→(23), l6→(24). The two brand marks TRIAGE apart: mark_A runs a genuine prep-before-trace chain straighten(25)→crisp(26)→crop_to_bounds(27)→remove_background(28)→vectorize(29)=harbor_logo.svg, while mark_B goes the other way crop_to_bounds(30)→remove_background(31)→crop_and_resize(32)=harbor_seal.png, deliberately never touching image_vectorize. font_recommend(33) consumes the brand kit. The six listing crops plus the two prepped marks converge into the upload session(34)→finalize(35)→document_merge_data_layout(36) with the authored .indd and the roster CSV, emitting one page per row and resolving @Photo (distinct per listing) / @Wordmark / @Seal (shared) per row; the merged set is exported ONCE by document_render_layout(37) to the single US-Letter proof book (six pages, one listing per page). Only the search and the supplied inputs originate outside the chain; nothing is upscaled or generatively expanded.
difficulty_rationale: Long-horizon flagship with difficulty from DEPTH, not breadth or plumbing: 37 connector calls, 15 distinct Adobe tools across three groups (asset_* stock+storage, image_* grade/straighten/crop/tint/vectorize/knockout, document_* merge/export), above the >=10 call / >=6 distinct-tool floor even after stripping the ingest, the two upload steps and the auto_straighten auto-op. The core is not a repeated recipe: six listing photos start on divergent casts across two colour axes (warm, cool+under, green-tint, mixed-split, underexposed, already-on-target) and there is no single correction that matches the set — the agent must diagnose each frame by eye off its in-frame grey card and apply divergent, differently-weighted corrections that all converge on one neutral card + one mid/whites/blacks target, then match-grade a SEPARATE licensed stock hero (which has no card) to the SAME white point on its own natural neutral so owned and licensed imagery read as one family. The house look is authored from primitive tone controls and held identical, not picked from a preset and not delegated to auto-tone. Layered on: seven web slots cut DOWN from the ~5000px graded hero master (distinct geometries, all downscales, a navy monochromatic promo variant among them); a two-way TRIAGE of the two brand marks under NEUTRAL names (the flat wordmark prepped-and-vectorized, the photographed embossed brass seal knocked to transparent raster because a trace would flatten its brass); prep-before-trace discipline on the skewed off-white wordmark scan; and a three-image-column one-record-per-page data-merge into a hand-authored single-record .indd that produces a single six-page featured-listings proof book (the agent-owned designed endpoint). Respects every hard limit: no generative fill/expand, no text-to-image, no upscaling (stock licensed large then cropped DOWN; listing photos camera-scale then cropped DOWN), no inpainting, no from-scratch layout; convert_pdf_to_indd is NOT used; document_render_layout makes ONE whole-document export, not a per-record export; image_crop_and_resize is downscale-only with onSubjectClipping='extract'; image_fill_area and image_apply_color_overlay are unused; deprecated image_adjust_color_temperature / _highlights / _vibrance_and_saturation are replaced by image_apply_adjustments; image_apply_monochromatic_tint is a valid whole-image tonal treatment on the square banner.
hardness_rationale: FAILURE GATE (a wrong DECISION, not a self-measurement): the six listing photos start under different light and must converge on ONE Harbor Crest house look, judged on the in-frame grey card each carries landing on one common neutral + one common mid-grey, whites held and blacks off pure black; the agent works BY EYE and REPORTS the per-frame white-balance / exposure it applied, and those moves must be NON-IDENTICAL — a set each 'auto-fixed' to look fine alone, or one global WB copied across the batch, or a per-frame auto-tone, visibly fails at the cards (the green kitchen stays green under any temperature-only move, and the warm and cool frames need opposite directions), and identical reported numbers are a visible fail. A second, undisclosed trap frame (listing_ref_06) already reads on the house warm-white and is correctly exposed, so the correct move is to HOLD white balance and only match tone — the brief says only 'match, don't overcook' and never discloses this, so a naive agent that warms everything to look 'golden and inviting' pushes its trim off-neutral and breaks the set. A third wrong-DECISION gate is the two-brand-mark TRIAGE under neutral names: the flat wordmark must be prepped-and-vectorized to clean line art while the photographed embossed brass seal must be knocked to transparency and KEPT as raster (a trace flattens its sheen to a muddy silhouette) — getting it backwards is invisible in a thumbnail and only shows when the seal prints dead. The merge adds a fourth checkable gate: page-count must equal roster row-count (6), since document_merge_data_layout is one-record-per-page. HUMAN-HARD ELEMENTS: (1) cross-asset consistency to a MEASURABLE target — six differently-lit owned listings all neutralised to their in-frame cards AND a card-less licensed stock hero match-graded to the same white point on its natural neutral, the counter-intuitive insight that a matched OUTPUT requires DIFFERENT per-frame corrections across two colour axes; (2) the two-way brand-mark triage needing different correct treatments; (3) prep-before-trace discipline (straighten→crisp→crop-to-bounds→knock-to-transparency) on the skewed off-white wordmark scan before vectorize; (4) the resolution discipline — stock licensed large and cropped DOWN to every web slot, listing photos camera-scale and cropped DOWN to the print @Photo frame at ~300 DPI, never an enlargement. TRAP the naive path falls into: 'apply one warm grade to everything' (fails at the cards and on the green kitchen), 'warm the golden exterior further' (breaks the on-target frame), 'trace both marks' (kills the brass seal), and 'trace the wordmark scan raw' (bakes in the paper and skew). MEASURABLE ACCEPTANCE (grader-side, the agent never measures): neutrality is graded on the SIX RETAINED card-bearing masters (grey card in frame) within a tight channel-spread tolerance with the mid patch on a shared mid-grey, whites below clipping and blacks off pure black; the delivered listing crops are checked separately for card-EXCLUSION; the stock hero's natural-neutral trim reads the same warm-white as the set; every web slot is at its exact listed pixel size and a downscale from the ~5000px master; each @Photo is a ~300 DPI downscale from a ~4000px source; the wordmark is a clean skew-free transparent-ground vector and the seal a transparent-ground raster >=300 px square with sheen intact (NOT vectorized); the agent reports non-identical per-frame corrections whose directions match each frame's cast (a tint move on the green kitchen, opposite temperature moves on the warm vs cool frames, white balance HELD on the on-target frame); and exactly one press-ready proof page per roster listing.
